issue_context.title: PVR frequently segfault's on startup...
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
... when trying to set GroupName but obtaining an instance for client id 0 fails. i believe client id 0 is invalid.
it happens frequently on startup and can be fixed by removing `TV38.db` so this one gets recreated.
lasted 16 days functional until crashing and the crash is reproducable. i saved the database files.
```
-rw-r--r--  1 nexus nexus   131072 16. Sep 19:25 TV38.db        <--- this is created new and functional
-rw-r--r--  1 nexus nexus   143360 31. Aug 16:35 TV38.db.crash  <--- this is not corrupted, can be accessed via sqlite3
-rw-r--r--  1 nexus nexus   143360 16. Sep 09:07 TV38.db.crash2
```

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
this setup with kodi master, pvr.hts and the tvheadend server is restarted dialy.. after 16 days it crashes on startup but no idea why (ok, client id 0 invalid)

### Debuglog
https://paste.kodi.tv/gehujasove.kodi

```
2021-09-16 18:59:47.325 T:1694    DEBUG <general>: AddOnLog: pvr.hts: event id:10004823 channel:12784202 start:1631829900 stop:1631831100 title:Tagesschau vor 20 Jahren desc:
2021-09-16 18:59:47.324 T:1695    DEBUG <general>: AddOnLog: pvr.hts: receive message [eventAdd]
2021-09-16 18:59:47.326 T:1700    ERROR <general>: Skipped 73 duplicate messages..
2021-09-16 18:59:47.324 T:1700    ERROR <general>: SetGroupName: Unable to obtain instance for client id: 0
```

## Additional context
a `TV38.db.crash` database is no problem for Matrix. it doesnt crash here.
i suspect that https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19831 introduced this.

trying a build before this merge commit (which is the merge of https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19786) the crash doesn't happen, even though a 'disfunctional' `TV38.db` is already on the filesystem.
however updating to current master after that also works fine. not sure how long it will.

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
<!--- Put your text below this line. Checkboxes can easily be ticked once issue is created -->
 - [X] Linux

 - Operating system version/name: Debian Bullseye
 - Kodi version: current master

With a note, I don't really understand here, is the following crash accepted and only the previous log entry as information from where?

The following `(*channel).second` would probably not work :thinking: .
Or has you forgot a `return false;` or `continue`?

Maybe on the log, add also the amount of channels, think good to know (not that for some reason 0 or 1 come):
```cpp
      CLog::Log(LOGERROR, "Cannot find group member '{},{}' in {} channels!", groupMember.first.first,
                groupMember.first.second, channels.size());
```

inconsistency of the TV database occurred twice with a distance of about 2 weeks at my end. both times after a clean shutdown of kodi. we didn‘t really find the root cause, but this pr corrects the db then and throws out the warning…

doesnt mean it can never happen again but it can cope with it now
The comment means that I want to crash (due to the following call to `(*channel).second`, yes. I also could assert() or throw. I forgot nothing and was hoping the comment makes the intention clear.
`const` has no effect here? Do you mean to just infer there is no need to change it, which is fine BTW.

> infer there is no need to change it

This. As you know I'm a big fan of Item 21 in Scott Meyers' book Effective C++ ("Use const whenever possible").
Such naked Lock/Unlock always give me a shiver... What are the thoughts on renaming these member functions to lowercase `lock` and `unlock` so that a `std::lock_guard` can be used?
This is something for another day/PR.
